name: Right Door, Wrong Exit
about: A single-page, click-through liminal-space walkthrough in the backrooms genre: an arcade-cabinet title card, then seven rooms, each a loading clip that glitches into a looping room video under a typewritten caption, then a first-person three.js walk to the room's exit. Plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript, no build step.

stages.title: Overview and the loop
prompts: In one sentence, what should the player feel when the loop returns them to the title card?
Is it a game, a walkthrough, or a piece to watch? Which word do you use for it?
Who is it for first: you, friends you send the link to, or strangers in the backrooms community?
What should this teardown help you decide next?

stages.title: Screens, glitches and the paper card
prompts: A loading screen is the clip and nothing else, for exactly five seconds. Why five, and why nothing over it?
The SKIP tab means no room is a dead end. Do you want people to use it?
Phone or desktop first: which one do you play it on yourself?

stages.title: The walk, the exits and the mini games
prompts: The mini games are bonuses: the exit is open from the start. Should any of them ever gate the exit?
Only three of the seven rooms have a mini game. Should the other four get one, or is the walk enough?
Which room is the best to walk, and which feels unfinished?

stages.title: The seven rooms and the story they tell
prompts: The captions and the logs tell a story of someone going deeper. Who is the narrator to you?
The four phases run from the Departure from Reality to the Empty Expanse. Is there a room missing between them?
Do the clock stamps (14:32 to ERR_CLOCK_NOT_FOUND) carry the story, or are they texture?

stages.title: Video, procedural rooms and sound
prompts: The room videos came first and the 3D rooms were built to match them. Which is the real room to you?
Every 3D sound is synthesized. Should the walk use the rooms' own audio tracks instead?
What should a room sound like when nothing is happening?

stages.title: Engine, phones and tests
prompts: What is the slowest phone it must run on?
The walk test runs in a browser with Playwright. Should it run on every push?
The case-sensitive file names collide on macOS and Windows. Rename them, or keep the pairs?

stages.title: How it was made, and what is next
prompts: It began as a click-through of videos and grew a 3D walk. Was that always the plan?
Ninety-Nine took this game as its structural reference. What did you carry over, and what did you leave behind?
What would make it finished, and what would make you stop?
